title: field-sampler-brief-lane-proposals-nov-2029
content:
Field Sampler Brief — lane proposals and quick experiments (working notes)

Context and purpose
- This note pulls together the recent tranche of frontline asks from pilot customers (APAC fintech, mid-market search SaaS, and an internal POC) observed between 2029-10-10 and 2029-11-04. Aim: identify 3–5 low-friction probes we can run with engineering in the next sprint to validate impact and unblock commonly requested outcomes (stable latency for bursts, simpler private deployment onboarding, cheaper embedding calls at scale).
- Tone: tactical. These are not final specs — they are intentionally lightweight proposals for micro-experiments that can produce quick data to inform roadmap bets.

Raw signal highlights (representative quotes)
- "When traffic spikes we see a 3–4x token cost for retries — need deterministic fallback behavior." — APAC fintech CX lead
- "Embedding costs are our dominant bill; batching heuristics are opaque and hard to configure safely." — Search SaaS product manager
- "Private deployment took 6 days to wire KMS and logs; we lost momentum with security reviewers." — Enterprise infra buyer
- "We want canary config for model variant fallbacks aligned with latency SLOs, not separate feature flags." — Platform engineering lead

Observed patterns and root causes (quick synthesis)
- Cost vs latency trade-offs: Many customers default to single-request low-batch settings to minimize tail latency, but this increases tokens served overall; lack of transparent per-route batching suggestions leads to conservative configs.
- Onboarding friction for Private: KMS onboarding and audit-log ingestion are frequent blockers; missing prebuilt templates for common KMS providers increases time-to-first-test.
- Fallback logic mismatch: customers want a declarative way to express fallback preferences (prefer lower-cost model unless latency > X) but our current rollouts/route config is orthogonal.
- Observability blind spots: customers ask for token-level cost breakdowns but also want sampling traces for KV cache hits — we collect traces but sampling is inconsistent.

Priority micro-probes (ranked for 2-week sprint feasibility)
1) Route-aware batching suggestion engine (probe):
   - What: lightweight rule-based advisor that suggests per-route batch_size and max_wait based on recent request size distribution and target p95 latency.
   - Why: immediate wins on unit cost without major infra changes; addresses the most common ask.
   - Quick metric: reduction in tokens-per-session and 95th percentile latency on pilot customers.
   - Rough estimate: 4 dev-days + 1 SRE day.
   - Owner: Evan Martinez.
   - Risk: bad default could increase tail latency; start with read-only suggestions and an opt-in toggle.

2) Private onboarding checklist + KMS connector templates (probe):
   - What: curated pack of KMS wiring scripts (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault) + a runbook that maps each step to audit artifacts we need for compliance review.
   - Why: removes the single largest time-sink reported by enterprise buyers; helps sales close faster.
   - Quick metric: onboarding time to first inference test (goal: <= 48 hours).
   - Rough estimate: 3 docs + 3 infra-days to create and test templates.
   - Owner: Sophia Patel.
   - Risk: maintenance burden; scope to most common customer setups only.

3) Canary fallback DSL (probe):
   - What: a minimal declarative syntax added to route configs to express fallback priorities and a simple runtime that enforces them (e.g., prefer-model-A unless p95 > 200ms then route to model-B).
   - Why: directly maps to customer desire for cost-aware graceful degradation.
   - Quick metric: successful failovers during capacity constraints and reduced SLA incidents.
   - Rough estimate: 6 dev-days + 2 QA-days.
   - Owner: Liam Chen.
   - Risk: needs careful testing to avoid feedback loops; include opt-in and metrics gating.

4) Sampling trace for KV cache hits (probe):
   - What: add a lightweight sampling flag that surfaces KV cache hit/miss at token granularity in existing traces (no new storage, stream to our debug window).
   - Why: customers repeatedly ask for evidence that cache strategies actually reduce inference work.
   - Quick metric: number of cache hits observed per 1k requests, correlation with latency/cost.
   - Rough estimate: 2 dev-days + 1 SRE-day.
   - Owner: Evan Martinez + SRE rotation.

Low-effort quick patches (can be triaged separately)
- Add visible per-route estimated cost-per-1000-requests in Console (UI stub + backend calc).(1 dev-day, 1 design-hour)
- Expose a single toggle to enable per-request token breakdown in hosted logs for 7 days (compliance opt-in).(2 dev-days)
- Create a customer-facing one-pager: "Best practices for embedding cost containment" (doc + checklist).(half day)

Open questions and unknowns
- How many customers will adopt advisor suggestions vs prefer platform to autotune? Need 2–3 pilot customers for early adoption metrics.
- Fallback DSL semantics: do we expose latency percentiles or absolute latency? Ask product/legal for SLO contract implications.
- KMS templates: how to handle air-gapped customers (on-prem HSM)? Might need a separate runbook.

Next steps and ask list
- Customer-success: pick 2 pilot accounts for the Route-aware batching suggestion engine. (Aisha)
- Engineering: spike the advisor as a read-only endpoint and deliver a UI suggestions view for review. (Evan, Liam)
- Security: review KMS runbook for any missing compliance docs and identify owners for Vault templates. (Sophia)
- Product: quick alignment meeting to decide whether the Canary DSL should be a config extension or a separate rollout object. (invite: product-hosted-api)

Internal notes to self (scratch)
- If advisor reduces tokens by >12% on pilot, prioritize auto-apply with conservative thresholds.
- Consider bundling KMS templates into an interactive bootstrapper in Console Q1.
- Track any escalation threads referencing JIRA-4821 and correlate to probe outcomes.

Appendix: quick telemetry snippets observed
- APAC fintech spike: median request size 560 tokens, p95 latency jumps from 120ms to 420ms under concurrent bursts (sample window: 2029-10-18 03:00–05:00 UTC).
- Search SaaS embedding pattern: 18% of calls have <= 16 tokens but are sent as singletons; batching could combine 3–5 requests and reduce per-call overhead.

Bottom line
- There are multiple low-friction experiments that directly map to customer pain: batching advice, KMS onboarding templates, fallback DSL, and KV trace sampling. Each can be scoped to deliver quick learnings and measurable lift. Start with the advisor (lowest ramp + highest impact) and KMS checklist (sales enablement).

-- end --
